description: Cycle-graph probes for n8n-workflow 2.9.1: the reference runtime has NO cycle validation (grep: 'cyclic' absent from reference/n8n packages/workflow/src and packages/core/src), so C-01/C-02 record that a cyclic workflow CONSTRUCTS and TRAVERSES fine; C-03 records the ADDITIVE validation LEGO (agent-4 workflow-rules.ts, ISSUE-003 Option A NEW CAPABILITY) flagging CYCLE_DETECTED. Sections are labelled; do not read C-03 as reference behaviour.
scopeWarning: The reference n8n 2.9.4 accepts cyclic workflows at construction and traversal. A port that rejects a cycle at construction or in plain traversal DIVERGES from the reference. Cycle detection exists only in the additive validator (and the Rust port's detect_cycles, which must match workflow-rules.ts, not the runtime).

C-01_runtime_constructs_cycle_no_start_n.reference: workflow.ts constructor (no cycle validation); getStartNode :867-883 (no STARTING_NODE_TYPES node, no trigger/poll node types)

C-02_traversal_is_cycle_safe.section: reference behaviour (Connection LEGO 1:1 port of common/*.ts + graph-utils.ts)

C-03_additive_validator_flags_cycle.section: NEW CAPABILITY — additive validator (agent-4 workflow-rules.ts), NOT reference behaviour
C-03_additive_validator_flags_cycle.reference: tests/reference/agent-4/validation/workflow-rules.ts detectCycles (ISSUE-003 Option A); Rust oracle: crates/n8n-validation detect_cycles lib.rs:48. FINDING (this task): validateWorkflow composes only checkNodeUniqueness + checkDanglingConnections (workflow-rules.ts :168) — its own detectCycles is never called, so validateWorkflow reports a 3-cycle workflow as valid:true. Probes target the composable directly.
